hero.h1: Fly the TBS Chupito free, in your browser

smallPrint: TBS Chupito: Nanawing’s recreation; its handling is not TBS flight data.

items.p: It rolls at 360°/s, the quickest roll in the hangar. Flick it from bank to bank between the gates with small stick inputs, so the real one doesn’t surprise you.
Open it up to 140 km/h on the straights. It stalls at 35 km/h and gives a stall warning at 44 km/h, so carry speed through the turns and ease it down gently when you land.

Windmill Run and River Run on the Island, Tunnel Run and Pyramid Run in the Desert, and Estate Run, 2.8 km through Parkland’s giant oaks and over the estate roofs: take the Chupito or the WUDFLY Spectre. Set a lap time, see where you rank, then go back and beat it.

controls.h2: Fly it with what you have
paragraphs: Keyboard, gamepad or your own USB RC radio on a laptop; two thumb sticks on your phone. No gaming PC: most laptops from the last few years run it.

On the keyboard a tap nudges the wing and a hold gives you full stick, so you can fly it clean without a radio. Press Space for a two-handed throw over your head and it’s away. Keep an eye on your battery on the iNAV-style OSD.

items: It stalls at 35 km/h. A slow, tight turn is the usual way to crash a Chupito. Keep the speed up and start the turn early.
The roll is quick. Small inputs, then wait; the wing does the rest.
Landing: ease it down and keep a little throttle in. Chop the throttle early and it drops.
Crash in the sim, then reset and go again. Repeat a manoeuvre until it’s clean, then take it to the field.

prints._about: Verified 23 Oct 2026 by reading each designer's page (MakerWorld and Thingiverse; both open in a browser). Printables and Cults3D also list Chupito parts but sit behind a bot check, so none are linked yet. Each `what` line paraphrases the designer's own description; `by` and `site` are the credit. Downloads at the time: wall hanger 238, fin slider 220, USB-C mount 156, VTX lock 122, servo cover 97.
prints.h2: Print the parts other pilots already designed
prints.intro: Each link goes to the designer’s own page on MakerWorld or Thingiverse, picked for downloads, reviews and clear notes. Check the fit on your own build before you print; electronics and shells differ.

groups.h3: Keep the camera and VTX where you put them

items.title: TBS Chupito 800 Pan-Tower
items.what: Pan the camera on a Feetech FT90M servo and look into the turn. It is the mount Team BlackSheep links from the kit page, and the designer links a DJI O4 Pro mount for it.

items.title: TBS Chupito camera pod with a lock
items.what: A camera pod that locks between the battery-tray ribs, so a hard throw can’t push the VTX assembly back. Lift the lock with a finger to take it out.

items.title: TBS Chupito VTX Cage lock
items.what: A 2 g TPU block that stops the stock VTX support sliding back when you throw.

items.title: TBS Chupito O4 Pro 10 degree soft mount
items.what: Soft-mounts a DJI O4 Pro on M2 gummies, tilts it 10° down and leaves room for ND filters.

groups.h3: A hatch and a battery that stay put

items.title: TBS Chupito Battery Holder
items.what: Lets shorter 5-inch quad packs sit tight under the stock strap. One version takes an Ummagrip plate, so the CG stays where you set it from pack to pack.

items.title: TBS Chupito Battery Tray 2 Stap
items.what: A TPU tray with two straps in the middle, for when the single stock strap won’t hold a balanced pack.

items.title: Screw Down Hatch for Team BlackSheep Chupito
items.what: Lost the foam hatch? This one screws down with an M3 instead of clipping. Stretch it 2 mm before printing; the page says why.

items.title: TBS Chupito Bottom Fin Slider
items.what: A skid for the bottom fin, so landings on tarmac wear the print and not the foam. Tape or hot-glue it on.

items.title: TBS Chupito Magnetic Wing Connectors
items.what: Slide the wings on with a magnetic click, no servo leads to plug in. Uses the spring-loaded 4-pin connectors the designer links.

items.title: Servo air cover TBS Chupito
items.what: Covers the servo arms. Print it in ASA or nylon and glue it on.

items.title: TBS Chupito FPV Wing USB-C Board Mount
items.what: Tape a USB-C board to the print and clip it into the bay, so the port stays reachable.

items.title: Chupito FC Deck
items.what: Replaces the plywood deck: 20×20 or 30.5 mounts for the flight controller, a slot to zip-tie the ESC underneath and a spot for the GPS at the back.

items.title: Wall Mount Hanger for TBS Chupito FPV Wing
items.what: Hang the wing on the wall by its motor with one screw. Needs the standard TBS electronics package.

logs.h2: Once yours is flying, replay the flight
paragraphs: If you’ve flown the real one, drop its log into the log viewer and watch it again on a 3D globe, with attitude, altitude, battery and signal alongside. See where the nose dropped before that wobble. Then check how far out the signal held and what the battery did on the long climb.
Drop in an iNAV or Betaflight blackbox log, or the telemetry CSV from your EdgeTX radio’s SD card. Free, in your browser, and the log never leaves your machine.

links.label: Turn on logging in EdgeTX, Betaflight or iNAV

items.q: Is this the real TBS Chupito?
items.a: It’s Nanawing’s recreation of Team BlackSheep’s 800mm wing, with the same span and shape. It is not an official TBS simulator. Practise the habits here; the kit itself comes from Team BlackSheep.

items.q: Do I need an RC radio?
items.a: No. Fly on the keyboard, a gamepad or your own USB RC radio. On the keyboard, a tap nudges and a hold gives full stick.

items.q: Does it work on a phone?
items.a: Yes. Open the same link on your phone and fly with two thumb sticks on the screen.

items.q: Is it free, and do I have to install anything?
items.a: It’s free and runs in your browser: no install, no login. After the first visit it works offline too.

items.q: Where can I buy a TBS Chupito in India?
items.a: Compare Chupito prices and stock at Indian hobby sellers on Wings, then buy from each seller’s page.

link.label: Compare TBS Chupito prices in India

items.q: Are there 3D-printed parts for the Chupito?
items.a: Yes. Pilots have shared a pan camera tower, battery holders, a screw-down hatch, a fin skid, magnetic wing connectors and more, free on MakerWorld and Thingiverse.

items.q: Can I watch my real Chupito flight back afterwards?
items.a: Yes. Drop in the iNAV or Betaflight blackbox log, or the EdgeTX telemetry CSV, and watch it on a 3D globe with the charts alongside. Free in your browser; the log stays on your machine.

faqNote: Sim time is no substitute for instruction, aircraft checks or safe flying at the field.
